0.0.n: 中 added to 勉強 indicates that studying is in progress.

0.1.n: Marks studying time as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: This is the name of a time management technique, written in katakana.

0.3.n: Connects the technique’s name to 手法, the general category it belongs to.

0.4.n: A somewhat formal noun for a way of doing something.

0.5.n: Marks 手法 as what the speaker uses.

0.6.n: The て-form of 意識する describes how the speaker uses the method: with deliberate awareness.

0.7.n: 使う + ている describes ongoing use; the final て connects this clause to what follows.

1.0.n: Combines with 時間 to specify time spent doing tasks.

1.1.n: 作業時間 refers to the duration of work sessions.

1.2.n: Marks work time as something divided by 区切って.

1.3.n: Gives the work interval; に is omitted here but appears after the parallel rest interval.

1.5.n: Combines with 時間 to refer to a break period.

1.6.n: 休憩時間 refers to the duration of breaks.

1.7.n: Marks rest time as another thing divided by 区切って.

1.8.n: Gives the length of each break; 分 counts minutes.

1.9.n: Marks the interval length resulting from dividing the time.

1.10.n: The て-form of 区切る connects dividing the time to the explanation that follows.

2.0.n: 力 adds the idea of ability or capacity to 集中, focusing.

2.1.n: Marks concentration as what is maintained.

2.2.n: 維持し is the connecting form of 維持する, used before ながら.

2.3.n: Attaches to 維持し to show that maintaining focus happens alongside advancing the work.

2.4.n: This describing word takes に to explain how the work progresses.

2.5.n: Turns 効率的 into a description of how an action is done.

2.6.n: Refers to the tasks being carried out, not a workplace or job title.

2.7.n: Marks 作業 as what the method helps move forward.

2.8.n: This form describes 時間管理法: a method that moves work forward.

2.9.n: Combines with 管理法 to specify what is being managed.

2.10.n: 管理 means management; 法 adds the sense of a method or system.

2.11.n: Links the noun 時間管理法 to explanatory んです.

2.12.n: A shortened の that presents the statement as an explanation.

2.13.n: Makes the explanation polite as part of なんです.

2.14.n: Although often meaning but, here it softly connects the explanation to the speaker’s recommendation.

3.0.n: A very casual intensifier, common in conversation.

3.1.n: With ある, this expresses effectiveness; the particle が is omitted in casual speech.

3.2.n: The plain form of ある combines with 効果 to say the technique produces results.

3.3.n: Follows the reason for the recommendation: the technique works very well.

3.4.n: A noun used with です to express that the speaker recommends something.

3.5.n: Adds politeness to the recommendation despite the casual めっちゃ earlier.

0.lit: During studying, I consciously use a method called the Pomodoro Technique, and…
0.tip: という places a name before a general noun: ポモドーロテクニックという手法 means a method called the Pomodoro Technique.

1.lit: Dividing work time into 25 minutes, rest time into five minutes, and…
1.tip: The final に区切って applies to both time periods, even though に is omitted after 25分.

2.lit: It is a time management method that advances work efficiently while maintaining concentration, and…
2.tip: ながら shows two actions happening together: maintaining concentration while moving work forward.

3.lit: Because it really has an effect, it is recommended.
3.tip: 効果ある is casual for 効果がある; speakers often drop が in conversation.
